finding.claim: Broken authorization on project deletion: the boolean-returning authorized() is called without checking its result, so any authenticated user can delete any project regardless of ownership.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending DELETE /projects/:id with another user's project id

trace.note: DELETE handler; id taken from req.params.id
project fetched by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized() returns true/false but the return value is discarded; it never throws (unlike authorize())

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 only returns a boolean and the result is ignored. No throw, no if-check, no middleware visible in this file. The sibling PUT route uses authorize(), which throws, confirming the intended pattern. Auth/req.user middleware is not in this repo, so only authentication, not ownership, can be assumed.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean only, and its result is discarded at api.js:18. There is no middleware in the repo, and no other file in the directory contains router.use, app.use or projects.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() as a bare statement, so the ownership check never blocks the delete at api.js:19. Any authenticated user can delete any project, unlike the PUT route at api.js:25, which uses the throwing authorize().

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean that is discarded at api.js:18; no middleware or other checks in the directory (api.js is the only file)
verdict_facts.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, whereas the PUT route at api.js:25 correctly uses the throwing authorize().
